Definition: a prolonged form of a primary verb, which is use only as an alternate in certain tenses; to take (in very many applications, literally and figuratively (properly objective or active, to get hold of; whereas G1209 is rather subjective or passive, to have offered to one; while G138 is more violent, to seize or remove)):--accept, + be amazed, assay, attain, bring, X when I call, catch, come on (X unto), + forget, have, hold, obtain, receive (X after), take (away, up).
BiblicalUsage: To take or receive is the great verb of getting, used two hundred and forty-three times for taking bread, taking a wife, and receiving the Spirit. In John 1:12 "as many as received him, to them gave he power to become the sons of God," in 1 Corinthians 2:12 "we have received, not the spirit of the world, but the spirit which is of God," and in 1 Peter 4:10 every man is to minister "the gift" he has received.
TheologicalSignificance: In my reading, the whole Christian life is in the verb: we receive Him, we receive His Spirit, and we receive gifts to give away, and nothing I have was not first received. I received Him, I received His Spirit, and I received gifts to give away.
